test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The sum of 6 times the present age of A and 4 times the present age of B is 156 years. 2 times the present age of B exceeds 9 times the present age of A by 30 years. What will be the sum of the ages (in years) of A and B, 9 years from now?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **A** and **B** be present ages.

Equation 1: 6A + 4B = 156 → 3A + 2B = 78

Equation 2: 2B − 9A = 30 → 2B = 9A + 30

Substitute 2B in Eq 1: 3A + (9A + 30) = 78 → 12A = 48 → A = 4 years.

Then 2B = 9(4) + 30 = 66 → B = 33 years.

Sum of ages after 9 years = (4 + 33) + (9 × 2) = 37 + 18 = 55 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 55 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ea9d70288cd4278e05282439c6ad3e82e0060c0c699a12388075c01ee6091fa.png] 

**Given:**

6A + 4B = 156 ... (i)

2B − 9A = 30 ... (ii)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divide (i) by 2: 3A + 2B = 78

⇒ From (ii): 2B = 30 + 9A

⇒ Substitute in simplified (i): 3A + (30 + 9A) = 78

⇒ 12A = 48

⇒ **A = 4 years**

⇒ 2B = 30 + 9(4) = 66

⇒ **B = 33 years**

⇒ Present sum = 4 + 33 = 37 years

⇒ Sum 9 years later = 37 + (9 + 9) = 55 years

**∴ The correct answer is 55 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Solving for unknown ages using **substitution** or **elimination** methods based on given conditions.

Age Sum Transformation

If there are 'n' persons, the sum of their ages after 't' years increases by **n × t**.

Ratio of Ages

The **difference** between the ages of two people always remains constant over time.</p
